description: Relay link frames (plan-1.0/03-protokol.md section 3). A frame is one binary WebSocket message: one type byte, then a UTF-8 JSON object. 'valid' vectors must decode to 'frame'; those with canonical=true must also re-encode to exactly 'hex' (fixed key order, no whitespace, JSON string escapes as produced by JSON.stringify). 'invalid' vectors must be rejected with the given error class. direction is the sender: client = host or device, relay = the relay. Numbers are safe integers only; counters travel as decimal strings. Frame type 0x10 DATA is reserved and rejected. Consumers must REJECT every invalid vector; the error names are the TypeScript reference classes and informative only (compare at most a coarse class: framing, encoding or shape). Rejection rules that other implementations must match: no duplicate keys at any depth, no unknown keys in envelopes, integers only (no fractions, exponents, '-0' or leading zeros; at most 2^53-1), no lone UTF-16 surrogates or invalid escapes, no raw control characters in strings, nesting depth at most 8. Nested 'args', 'data' and 'state' objects keep member insertion order: a Rust codec needs serde_json with the 'preserve_order' feature (or an ordered map) to re-encode the canonical vectors byte for byte.
